A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation and orientation-estimation experiments, dataset-curation analysis, ablations, and qualitative application results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical experiments and adds a no-LGM comparison and qualitative results on internet photographs and multi-object inputs.

M1.justification: The Trellis fine-tuning, Wonder3D LoRA/pixel-injector/LGM pipeline, and FoundationPose–DINO orientation estimation remain unchanged. Seven-view attention dimensions and DINOv2 patch feature maps clarify existing components. The no-LGM variant is an experimental ablation.

E1.justification: v2 Figures 7–8 extend qualitative evaluation to additional internet photographs and a multi-object scene containing several cars. Objaverse-OA training coverage and the GSO, Toys4k, and ImageNet3D benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces the internal comparison variant 'Wonder3D-OA (ours small)' with 'Wonder3D-OA (ours w/o LGM)'. The external comparator sets remain unchanged, including PCA, Gemini-2.0, Orient Anything, and FSDetView in their corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Table 1 replaces a reduced-training-data configuration with a control omitting LGM. Retained benchmark sample counts, training budgets, and metrics are unchanged. Appendix A.2 newly documents rendering viewpoints and Chamfer-distance handling; v1 does not specify these details sufficiently to establish a corresponding protocol change.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds a test of LGM's contribution but removes Wonder3D's reduced-category ablation. Trellis's reduced-category experiment remains in Table 2. Appendix analyses of geometry preservation, occlusion, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises retained Wonder3D comparisons' appearance scores and PCA geometry scores; full-model GSO LPIPS/CLIP changes from 0.2338/78.26 to 0.2270/80.30. Table 2 changes Trellis+PCA CD from 0.0912 to 0.0798 on GSO and 0.1031 to 0.0911 on Toys4k. The no-LGM row and Figures 7–8 add results; orientation-estimation tables remain unchanged. Unspecified earlier rendering details prevent interpreting appearance-score revisions as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The generative-model equations, rotation-error definition, and arrow-to-3D rotation construction are retained. No substantive mathematical definition, derivation, assumption, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: cross-category orientation-aligned generation, Objaverse-OA, adaptation of two generative backbones, and two downstream applications.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 explicitly extends stated applicability to internet photographs and multi-object inputs. Appendix A.2 adds the explanation that orthogonal-view evaluation would favor Wonder3D-OA, motivating spherical sampling. Existing occlusion limitations and failure explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents ImageNet3D-based conventions for ambiguous orientations, the pixel injector's six-to-seven-view attention dimensions, DINOv2 patch features, official Wonder3D++/Trellis checkpoints, and backbone-specific metric-rendering procedures. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes. Hardware, training budgets, and access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Jin et al.'s 'One-shot 3D Object Canonicalization Based on Geometric and Semantic Consistency' and distinguishes its intra-category Canonical Objaverse dataset from this paper's inter-category alignment. The other cited works are retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanations, more specific appendix cross-references, and an acknowledgements section, and replaces the preprint notice with a NeurIPS 2025 notice. The main narrative and appendix organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 7–8, resizes the Figure 1 overview, changes Table 1's ablation-row label, and relocates several retained figures and tables during reflow. Most visual content and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through clearer canonicalization, checkpoint, feature, and evaluation details, and adds a useful LGM control and broader qualitative examples. These gains are limited by the removed Wonder3D reduced-data ablation, which Section 6.2 still incorrectly cites, and incomplete explanation of the numerical revisions. The core methods and most evidence remain stable.
